dedupe_keys.name: ushant ais dataset of vessel trajectories brittany traffic separation scheme

description: The Ushant AIS dataset holds six months of Automatic Identification System records of vessels in the Ushant traffic separation scheme off Brittany in western France, one of the densest shipping areas in the world, with two separated navigation lanes. It mixes fast cargo ships and tankers on straight routes with slow sailing and fishing boats on varied headings. The whole set has 18,603 trajectories and more than 7 million position observations; only trajectories with more than 30 points were kept, and the time between consecutive observations ranges from 5 seconds to 15 hours, with 95% below 3 minutes. It was prepared for research on clustering segmented trajectories in continuous time, and the authors ask users to cite that article. Coverage: the Ushant area. Format and access: a single ZIP file of about 131 MB on figshare, without registration. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: a fixed six-month sample with no vessel identities described on the page and no port calls. It supports traffic flow and exposure studies of busy sea lanes, such as collision risk or route disruption models. It relates to Marine Cadastre AIS, the Danish AIS data and the AMSA vessel traffic data in the catalogue.
